payload.reason: The evidence provides specific methods and metrics used to measure the quality of word vectors, including correlation with human judgment and cosine similarity.

claims.text: The quality of word vectors is measured using the Pearson correlation coefficient, which assesses the correlation between human judgment of word similarity and the cosine distances between word vectors.
Cosine similarity is used to determine the most semantically similar word to a given stem word, indicating the quality of the word vectors based on their ability to capture semantic relationships.
Word vectors are evaluated through tasks like word analogy, where the ability to predict relationships between words reflects their quality.
